conceptZh: 廚師動物的麵團不肯過來，揮擀麵棍把麵團擀成來字，麵團終於跑過來。
object: a rotund chef animal in a tall hat, a rebellious ball of dough and a rolling pin
creativeAngle: 道具反抗：麵團自己跳走、黏住擀麵棍，廚師用麵粉當誘餌才把麵團請過來，擀開成來。
promptEn:
An 8-second clip on a pale butter backdrop with a soft pink tiled floor. A rotund cartoon chef bear in a tall white hat flings dough with far more confidence than accuracy, beside a ball of dough with its own opinions. The off-screen voice, warm and clear Taiwanese Mandarin, says exactly: 「來、來、過來」 (ㄌㄞˊ、ㄌㄞˊ、ㄍㄨㄛˋ ㄌㄞˊ), slowly with clear tones, then stops.
0.0-1.7s: The chef waves a paw, beckoning, but the dough ball hops away from him toward the far corner. 「來」 (ㄌㄞˊ) is spoken as he beckons.
1.7-3.4s: He tosses the rolling pin; the dough sticks to it and flies in a circle, the chef spinning; he sprinkles flour trail as bait.
3.4-4.4s: The dough finally follows the flour, rolls flat under the pin, and unrolls into thick strips that settle into a saturated solid chestnut-brown glyph 來, about 70% of frame height, with a horizontal in the middle and two little dots on each side of the center. The second 「來」 (ㄌㄞˊ) lands. 
4.4-5.0s: A small dough bunny hops across the stage toward the chef, and he catches it; 「過來」 (ㄍㄨㄛˋ ㄌㄞˊ) is spoken as it hops over.
5.0-8.0s: Hold: glyph 來 completely still and centered. The chef bows with his hat falling off, bunny dancing in the corner, never touching the strokes.
No text except the glyph 來; no subtitles, watermark or flashing. Soft music under the voice.

conceptZh: 太空人玩偶在遠處招手叫賽車「過來」，賽車衝過頭撞牆，再助跑趴地滑行像保齡球撞倒一排泡棉瓶，瓶子翻滾堆成「來」字，賽車最後真的跑過來煞車停在太空人身邊。
object: a row of eight chunky soft foam bowling pins standing across the middle of a glossy floor, with a bouncy astronaut toy beckoning from the far side
morph: the race car belly-slides into the pins like a bowling ball; the pins fly, spin and land stacked in a heap that fuses into the solid red strokes of 來 — one pin lying flat as the top horizontal, one standing tall as the center vertical, two short pins splayed on each side as the small 人 pairs, one pin as the lower horizontal and two tilted pins as the left and right legs
creativeAngle: 改走純肢體笑點：捨棄前一版「麵團不肯過來」的安靜變形，改成賽車助跑趴地滑行的保齡球全倒。第一次衝過頭撞牆（符合賽車愛衝過頭的個性），第二次全倒讓瓶子翻滾堆成「來」字，最後「過來」一詞由賽車真的跑向招手的太空人演出來，聽到的字和看到的動作同一件事。
promptEn:
An 8-second stylized toy animation on a pale cream backdrop with a glossy mint-green floor that looks slippery as a bowling lane. Only three things on screen: the lead, a row of pins, and one buddy. The lead is 賽車, a squeaky pull-back toy race car, cherry red with big googly eyes, who always overshoots and crashes nose first. The buddy is a bouncy astronaut toy in a fishbowl helmet who keeps floating off the floor at the wrong moment. Across the middle of the floor stand eight chunky soft foam bowling pins in a neat row, all the same warm tomato-red. A warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, slowly and distinctly with clear tones, reading exactly these syllables and nothing else: 「來、來、過來」 (ㄌㄞˊ、ㄌㄞˊ、ㄍㄨㄛˋ ㄌㄞˊ). No other dialogue, no subtitles, no on-screen text except the finished glyph 來.

0.0-1.5s (want it): The astronaut stands at the far right, waving both arms in a big "come here" beckon. The race car at the far left locks its googly eyes on the astronaut, scrapes backward on the floor to wind up its pull-back motor with a squeaky ratchet sound, wheels chattering. The first 「來」 (ㄌㄞˊ) is spoken exactly as the astronaut beckons and the car winds up.

1.5-3.0s (try and miss): The car launches far too fast, zips straight past the row of pins without touching a single one, overshoots the astronaut, and BONKs nose first into a soft padded wall at the right edge. It squashes flat, springs back, and rolls backward dizzy with spinning eyes. The astronaut, startled, drifts up off the floor and gently bonks its helmet on a hanging paper lantern, then floats back down.

3.0-4.5s (the big crash): The car shakes it off, backs up to the far left for a longer wind-up, freezes one beat with narrowed eyes, then charges, hops into the air and dives onto its belly, sliding across the slippery floor like a bowling ball with a long squeak. It plows into the row of pins. STRIKE: all eight foam pins fly upward, tumbling and spinning in a cloud of cartoon stars while the car skids to a stop just past them.

4.5-5.5s (the payoff): The pins drop and land in a heap that is the glyph. One lies flat as the top horizontal, one stands tall as the central vertical, two short pins splay on each side of the vertical as the small 人 pairs, one lies flat as the lower horizontal, and two tilted pins become the left-falling and right-falling legs. As they settle they fuse into clean, saturated solid tomato-red strokes forming a correctly written, standard Traditional Chinese 來, centered, uncropped, about 70% of frame height with clear margins. The second 「來」 (ㄌㄞˊ) is spoken exactly as the strokes snap into place.

5.5-8.0s (final hold): The glyph 來 stays perfectly still and readable for the full 2.5 seconds plus the settle before it. In the lower right corner, well clear of the strokes, the astronaut floats down and beckons again with both arms. 「過來」 (ㄍㄨㄛˋ ㄌㄞˊ) is spoken exactly as the race car zips along the bottom edge from left to right toward the astronaut and, for once, skids to a perfect stop right beside it. The car rears up on its back wheels in a proud strike pose, googly eyes spinning happily, then wobbles and gently bumps the astronaut, who floats up an inch and bobs back down. Neither ever touches or covers the glyph.

Bright, warm lighting, no pure white blowouts, no dark grading. Cartoon squash-and-stretch, soft toy sounds, soft music quieter than the voice. No watermark, no flashing, no extra text.
